bill.title: Campaign finance: public disclosure; disclosure of payments for social media posts; require, and require certain information be included in social media posts. Amends secs. 12 & 43 of 1976 PA 388 (MCL 169.212 & 169.243) & adds sec. 59a.

posted_text:
💰 MI SB 1199 — Michigan Wants You to Know: Social Media Ads for Campaigns Must Be Clear

Michigan is changing how political campaigns use social media.

Starting April 1st, any money spent on a social media post supporting or opposing a candidate or ballot question must be clearly disclosed.

Committees and independent contractors using social media to advertise need to include their name and address in the post itself, or with a clear disclaimer.

The post must also meet specific requirements depending on the type of media – at least 4 seconds for video, large lettering for graphics, and a clear audio statement.

Violations can result in fines of up to $1,000 for first offenses and $1,000 per violation for repeat offenses.

This new rule applies to committees, agents, and independent contractors, but doesn’t affect regular news publications or satirical content.

Oct. 6, 2026: Senate Co-sponsor(s) Named: Mallory Mcmorrow.
